title: Ranh giới dịch vụ và HTTP
requirements: Two independent Catalog/Orders processes communicate through HTTP; Orders owns snapshots and integer-cent totals.
Validate input and bounded payloads, distinguish dependency outage/timeout, use real HTTP integration tests.

title: Hợp đồng API và tương thích phiên bản
requirements: Build an independently runnable Catalog/Orders lesson with GET /v1/products/:id and a different nested-price /v2/products/:id schema; Orders continues consuming v1.
A pure runtime v1-product parser accepts additive unknown response fields but rejects missing/wrong-type/id/price fields; write meaningful unit fixtures first.

Prove compatibility with additive provider fields and rejection of incompatible upstream data over real HTTP with separate provider/consumer processes. Explain that TypeScript alone does not validate network JSON.

title: Dữ liệu thuộc từng dịch vụ
requirements: Use built-in node:sqlite for separate service-owned SQLite files under configurable temporary/data paths; never share a database file between services.
Demonstrate an order surviving Orders restart and retrieval without the Catalog dependency; use real processes and independent temp database paths per test.
Document schema/migration initialization, ownership boundaries and SQLite single-node tradeoffs, without claiming a production deployment.

title: Truyền deadline và hủy yêu cầu
requirements: Go beyond lesson01 single-hop timeout: propagate a bounded end-to-end remaining deadline through Gateway→Orders→Catalog.
Use AbortController and validated deadline metadata; cancel downstream work when the caller disconnects or the budget expires.
Unit-test budget calculations with an injected clock; use real service processes and synchronization/barriers to verify cancellation without brittle sleep-based assertions.

title: Tạo đơn có idempotency
requirements: Implement an Idempotency-Key contract for order creation with persistent service-owned SQLite records and a request fingerprint.
Concurrent identical requests return the same order; a reused key with different input returns409; a completed response can be replayed after restart.
Test real concurrent HTTP requests, conflict cases, input validation and restart recovery; explain failures still requiring recovery rather than asserting exactly-once networking.

title: Retry có giới hạn và backoff
requirements: Implement bounded retry policy with exponential backoff and jitter for transient safe/idempotent operations only, respecting the overall deadline.
Pure policy tests use deterministic RNG/clock; real HTTP tests make an upstream fail twice then succeed and prove exact bounded attempts.
Do not retry arbitrary POST requests blindly; compare safe GET and a request protected by an idempotency contract.

title: Circuit breaker và half-open
requirements: Build an explicit closed/open/half-open state machine around a downstream HTTP dependency; bound the half-open probe count.
Unit-test state/time transitions with an injected clock; integration-test fast failures while open and recovery after a successful probe.
Explain circuit breaker versus timeout/retry and document the scope/limits of per-instance state.

title: Correlation ID và log có cấu trúc
requirements: Propagate a validated correlation/request ID between independent HTTP services, using generated IDs for absent/invalid input.
Emit structured JSON logs without request secrets and demonstrate tracing one request across services.
Test interleaved requests for context isolation and actual propagated HTTP headers/log records; explain logs are not a full distributed tracing system.

title: API gateway và kết quả một phần
requirements: Build a gateway that concurrently aggregates two independently owned downstream resources through HTTP, without database sharing.
Set bounded per-dependency/overall deadlines and specify an explicit partial-result contract versus total failure.
Test healthy, single-dependency failure, total failure and input validation with real separate processes; avoid a gateway that reimplements all business logic.

title: Readiness và graceful shutdown
requirements: Extend beyond basic listener close: implement a draining state that rejects new business requests, reports readiness false, and lets in-flight work finish before a bounded exit.
Use a local lifecycle implementation if root shared helper semantics do not fit; do not modify root helpers.
Unit-test lifecycle transitions and integration-test SIGTERM with synchronized in-flight requests and eventual process exit; distinguish liveness and readiness.

title: Transactional outbox và giao nhận ít nhất một lần
requirements: Use a service-owned SQLite transaction to atomically store a business change and an outbox event.
Deliver events to another service over an explicitly documented HTTP transport with retries and an idempotent consumer; do not claim to implement Kafka or exactly-once delivery.
Test receiver outage, duplicate delivery and producer restart recovery with separate service processes and durable temp files.

title: Saga và hành động bù trừ
requirements: Build a small durable orchestrated saga coordinating simulated Inventory and Payment services over HTTP, without any real payment/network integration.
Document forward and compensating operations, idempotency and explicit recovery from failed compensation.
Test success, payment refusal, compensation and restart recovery using independent processes; do not call local compensation a distributed ACID transaction.

title: Bulkhead và cô lập tải giữa các dependency
requirements: Build an independently runnable gateway and two downstream HTTP services with separate bounded per-dependency concurrency pools; reject excess work promptly with an explicit 503 contract rather than an unbounded queue.

Unit-test admission, idempotent release, configuration validation and release after success, errors and cancellation; acquire capacity before starting downstream work and always release it in finally.

Use real independent processes and synchronization barriers to fill one dependency pool, prove rejected calls never reach that dependency, and prove the other dependency remains usable; verify capacity returns after failure and deadline cancellation. Explain per-instance scope and distinguish bulkheads from circuit breakers and rate limits.

title: Rate limiting bằng token bucket
requirements: Build an independently runnable gateway and downstream service; use a token bucket per validated bounded demonstration client ID, explicit capacity/refill configuration, and HTTP 429 with a positive integer Retry-After when the client exhausts its budget. Reject before forwarding and never present an untrusted demo header as authentication.

Use an injected monotonic clock for deterministic unit tests covering initial burst, refill boundaries, retry delay rounding, invalid configuration and client isolation. Bound client-tracking memory with a documented full-capacity policy; idle expiry may remove only buckets that would already have fully refilled, so eviction cannot reset a depleted client's quota.

Use real independent HTTP processes to prove exact admitted/rejected requests through downstream counters, client isolation, validation and Retry-After responses. Explain per-instance limits, process restart resets, replica multiplication and why rate limiting does not bound concurrent slow requests.

title: CQRS và read model nhất quán cuối cùng
requirements: Build independent Orders command and query/read-model processes with separate service-owned SQLite files. Orders atomically persists business state and durable event records; synchronize a query-optimized order summary over bounded HTTP requests without sharing database files or importing previous lessons.

Apply events and durable deduplication/checkpoint state atomically at the read model; define event IDs, per-order versions and explicit duplicate, conflicting and stale/out-of-order event contracts. Explain an explicit strategy for gaps rather than silently advancing past missing data.

Write meaningful pure policy or in-memory SQLite unit tests first. With real service processes, durable temporary files and synchronization barriers, prove observable stale reads while propagation is paused, eventual convergence, duplicate/version handling and producer/consumer restart recovery without double-counting. Document source-of-truth ownership, freshness metadata, bounded failures and why CQRS neither requires event sourcing nor guarantees immediate read-your-writes.

title: Cache-aside, TTL và chống cache stampede
requirements: Build independently runnable Catalog and cached-reader HTTP processes. Catalog owns source data; the reader uses a bounded in-memory cache with explicit TTL, eviction and stale-data semantics, validates upstream JSON, and has a bounded downstream deadline. Do not share stores or claim cache data is authoritative.

Coalesce concurrent misses for the same key into one bounded upstream load. Bound both cached entries and distinct in-flight loads; reject overload explicitly, release failed loads, and never cache exceptions as successful values. Use an injected clock and deferred promises for deterministic unit tests of exact expiry, eviction, coalescing, failure cleanup and capacity limits.

With real separate HTTP processes and synchronization barriers, prove cache hits avoid upstream work, simultaneous misses cause one upstream call, source changes remain stale only under the documented policy, failed loads can recover, and overload/deadline behavior is bounded. Document per-instance state, restart resets, invalidation tradeoffs and when caching is inappropriate.

title: Job bất đồng bộ lưu bền và HTTP 202
requirements: Build independent job API/owner and worker processes communicating only over HTTP. The API owns a SQLite job database; POST returns202 with Location and Retry-After, a bounded status endpoint distinguishes queued/running/succeeded/failed states, and completed results have an explicit retrieval contract. Use a deterministic local computation rather than external side effects.

Persist admission and transitions; use atomic claims with a bounded lease and a fencing/claim token so an expired worker cannot complete a reclaimed job. Bound job admission and attempts; terminal failures stay inspectable. Test transition, lease-boundary, stale-token and retry policy with an injected clock and in-memory SQLite before implementation.

Use real API and worker processes, separate temporary paths and synchronization barriers to prove asynchronous acceptance/polling, success, terminal failure, competing workers and recovery after a worker dies and its lease expires, including rejection of stale completion. Document at-least-once computation, result retention, wall-clock lease limitations and why202 is not completion.

title: Danh tính dịch vụ, token ký và phân quyền
requirements: Build independent caller and protected-resource HTTP processes demonstrating a small documented compact JWS/JWT profile signed with Ed25519 using node:crypto, never homemade cryptographic primitives. Pin EdDSA, an explicit token type, trusted issuer/audience and an allowlisted public key ID. Require safe-integer iat/nbf/exp seconds with iat<=nbf<=now<exp and exp-iat<=60, zero clock leeway, and an explicit service identity/scope policy. Never trust keys or URLs supplied by a token.

Use only throwaway locally generated demonstration key material, with no credential-store access, cloud identity provider or real secrets. Validate token size/shape, canonical base64url, signature, algorithm/type, key ID, issuer/audience and time claims before authorization. Distinguish missing/invalid authentication401 from valid identity lacking permission403; keep tokens and keys out of logs/errors. Use an injected clock for deterministic boundary and tampering unit tests.

With real separate HTTP processes prove allowed calls, absent/tampered/expired/wrong-audience tokens and denied scopes, plus rejecting unknown keys and algorithm confusion. Include fail-closed configuration checks and document that this is an educational narrow verifier, not a general JWT library, OAuth server or production identity system; bearer replay and transport confidentiality require controls outside this loopback HTTP demo, and production needs TLS and a maintained standards implementation.

title: Metrics HTTP, histogram và cardinality có giới hạn
requirements: Build independently runnable gateway and downstream HTTP processes with per-process request counters, active-request gauges and a classic cumulative duration histogram exposed in documented Prometheus text format. Use Node built-ins only; no monitoring server, package or deployment is required.

Use bounded allowlisted route templates, methods and outcome/status labels; never label by raw URL, resource ID, request ID or client-provided values. Record completion exactly once across response finish/close, include dependency failures and caller disconnects, and exclude or clearly separate scrape traffic. Unit-test injected-clock observations, cumulative buckets including +Inf, count/sum, escaping and idempotent completion.

Use real independent processes to scrape both services over HTTP, compare exact business-request counters, synchronize concurrent work to observe an in-flight gauge, and prove cleanup after error/cancellation and bounded series under varied unknown paths. Explain rates over time, instance restart resets, safe aggregation, histogram approximation and why per-process metrics alone do not constitute an SLO/alerting platform.

title: Strangler Fig và chuyển quyền sở hữu từng bước
requirements: Build independent facade, original legacy application and extracted service processes, with the two providers owning separate SQLite databases. Demonstrate an incremental migration with explicit legacy-only, copy/cutover and extracted-owner phases while the facade preserves one public contract; do not share a database or dual-write business changes.

Define a deterministic, durable migration/ownership policy that prevents new writes during a bounded copy/cutover barrier, drains previously admitted legacy writes before taking the copy snapshot, validates copied data and resumes safely after interruption. After cutover exactly one provider owns writes and reads follow the same owner; routing must not silently fall back to a stale provider after an uncertain write. Unit-test legal/illegal phase transitions, route ownership and interruption recovery policy first.

Use real separate HTTP processes, temporary databases and a synchronized already-in-flight legacy write to prove unchanged public API behavior before/after migration, new writes during cutover rejected explicitly, data preservation, restart recovery and failure of the extracted owner without writes leaking back to legacy. Keep this a small original teaching application, document the facade bottleneck, migration downtime/data-volume limits and rollback requirements after new writes, and distinguish strangler migration from gateway aggregation.

title: Service discovery và cân bằng tải phía client
requirements: Build independent registry, Catalog instance and client HTTP processes. Run two instances from one Catalog entrypoint; the client resolves a logical service through the registry and uses deterministic round-robin across live registrations. Use bounded renewable leases, bounded registry capacity, validated instance IDs and loopback-only demo URLs; never follow caller-supplied arbitrary URLs. At most four manifest entrypoints.

Write deterministic injected-monotonic-clock unit tests first for exact lease expiry, renewal, removal, capacity and round-robin membership changes. Define safe registration ownership so a stale renewal/removal cannot replace or delete a newer incarnation. All HTTP calls have bounded deadlines; no automatic retries of unsafe writes, no unbounded stale registry cache, and explicit 503 when discovery has no usable instances.

Use real independent processes to prove requests reach both instances, deregistration/lease expiry removes an instance, a terminated instance causes a bounded failure, and recovery/membership refresh uses a replacement without routing indefinitely to stale addresses. Use synchronization or bounded observable polling rather than fragile sleeps. Document registry outage and single-point-of-failure tradeoffs; a lease is not proof an instance is healthy, and this local teaching registry is not DNS/Consul/Kubernetes.

title: Optimistic concurrency với ETag và If-Match
requirements: Build an independently runnable resource-owner HTTP service with service-owned SQLite and a separate HTTP client/editor process. GET returns a strong ETag tied to a durable resource version. Two clients read the same version and attempt updates: atomically compare-and-update version and data so exactly one wins and the other receives412 with no lost update; never automatically replay a conflicting mutation.

Document a deliberately narrow conditional-update contract: require exactly one strong version ETag in If-Match for PUT/PATCH, missing precondition428, unsupported/malformed header400 and stale valid version412. Validate input and integer version bounds; failed validation/preconditions never change data/version. Unit-test parsing and atomic store behavior first, including weak/wildcard/list headers and version exhaustion. Explain the narrow header profile rather than claiming full RFC conditional-request support.

With real owner and client processes and temporary SQLite, synchronize two updates against one ETag and assert one success, one412, exactly one version increment and the winning value. Prove retrieval after restart retains value/version, a client can explicitly re-read and revise a later update, and failures/dependency deadlines have explicit contracts. Distinguish optimistic concurrency from idempotency, distributed locks and multi-service transactions.

title: Distributed tracing và quan hệ span qua nhiều dịch vụ
requirements: Build independent Gateway, Orders and Catalog HTTP processes propagating W3C traceparent through each hop. Demonstrate a documented version00 teaching profile: validate header shape, nonzero trace/span IDs and flags, generate fresh context on absent/invalid input, keep the trace ID across hops and generate distinct span IDs with explicit parent relationships. Use node:crypto and AsyncLocalStorage; do not claim to implement an OpenTelemetry SDK/exporter or full W3C version negotiation.

Write meaningful unit tests first with injected IDs/monotonic clock for parsing, parent-child construction, sampled-flag handling and span completion exactly once on finish/close/error. Emit bounded-size structured span records with allowlisted operation names, duration/status/outcome, without request bodies, authorization data or raw query strings. Explain traceparent versus tracestate, local clock durations versus cross-host clock ordering, and privacy/trust limits of caller-provided context.

With real independent processes, prove one request creates a connected parent-child tree across all three services, parallel/interleaved requests never mix contexts, valid inbound context is continued and invalid context creates a fresh trace. Synchronize a slow dependency and demonstrate its duration/error span; prove deadline/disconnect cleanup and exactly-once span completion. Use bounded local observation/log capture, no external collector or runtime dependency. Distinguish this from lesson08 correlation IDs and lesson19 aggregate metrics.

title: Thay đổi schema bằng Expand, Migrate và Contract
requirements: Build an original Catalog service with old/new executable versions and a migration/control entrypoint, using a single Catalog-owned SQLite database. Other business services never read its file. Demonstrate durable expand, resumable bounded backfill/migrate and contract phases for replacing a field while the HTTP business meaning remains stable. Old/new binaries represent versions/replicas of the same data owner, not independently owned services sharing a database.

Choose and document an explicit compatibility/write synchronization mechanism so old-version writes during backfill cannot be lost or leave new fields stale. Bound each backfill batch, commit progress atomically with row changes and safely resume after interruption. Forbid destructive contract while an old version can still write: use a real enforced retirement/admission barrier that drains admitted writes, not merely an unchecked user boolean. After contract old code must fail closed; rollback is supported only within its stated compatibility window. Unit-test phase guards, backfill interruption and concurrent-write preservation first.

Use real separate old/new service processes and HTTP requests with temporary SQLite and barriers to prove compatibility before contract, a concurrent old write survives backfill, interrupted backfill resumes without omissions, early contract is rejected, old writer retirement/drain is enforced, and new code works after contract/restart. Explain SQLite DDL locking, any bounded maintenance window, migration ownership and irreversible cleanup; do not claim production zero downtime or distributed dual-write atomicity.

title: Event sourcing, replay và snapshot có thể dựng lại
requirements: Build independent cart event-owner and reader HTTP processes. The owner stores immutable intent events in its own SQLite append-only stream; the reader obtains events only over bounded HTTP and reconstructs state without sharing the database. Model a small local cart with creation, item additions/removals and checkout, integer quantities and no real payment. The event stream is authoritative; snapshots are optional derived accelerators that can be discarded and rebuilt.

Write pure reducer/command and in-memory SQLite unit tests first for deterministic replay, domain invariants, event schema/version/sequence validation and expected-version appends. Atomically append against the expected stream version so concurrent conflicting commands cannot both commit. Bound carts, events per stream, page/batch sizes and operation deadlines. Define duplicate command handling or an explicit no-blind-retry contract; replay must never execute network/business side effects. Include a validated derived snapshot with fallback to full replay on unusable snapshot and explain its trust/invalidation limits.

Use real independent processes to prove command/history/state contracts, concurrent expected-version conflicts, restart reconstruction and reader reconstruction from paged events. Prove discarding snapshots yields identical state and malformed/out-of-order history is rejected rather than silently applied; document schema evolution/upcasting boundaries, replay cost and when CRUD is simpler. Distinguish event sourcing from lesson11 outbox and lesson15 CQRS; do not claim exactly-once delivery or cross-aggregate transactions.

title: Dead-letter queue, poison message và redrive có kiểm soát
requirements: Build independent durable queue-owner, consumer and idempotent sink HTTP processes with separate service-owned SQLite files. Focus on poison-message quarantine and operator redrive beyond lesson17 job terminal failure: transient failures have a finite attempt budget and poison messages enter an inspectable dead-letter state with a bounded allowlisted reason; an unrelated valid message can still complete. A manual bounded HTTP processing step is sufficient; no external broker or background polling is required.

Preserve original message ID and payload across redrive, and keep durable attempt/redrive audit counters. Redrive is an explicit conditional transition from dead-letter to queued, with a finite redrive-cycle limit; concurrent or stale redrive requests cannot reset active work or create duplicate queue entries. Claims need bounded leases and fencing so stale completions fail, and uncertain sink responses must not justify duplicate business effects: the sink atomically deduplicates by operation ID plus payload fingerprint. Bound queue admission, payloads, batches and processing concurrency. Write meaningful policy/in-memory SQLite unit assertions first.

Use real independent processes and temporary databases to prove poison isolation, attempts exhausted into DLQ, inspection, restart persistence, stale/concurrent redrive rejection and successful reprocessing only after an explicit simulated handler fix, without changing the message identity or data. Prove a lost/duplicate delivery cannot double-apply the sink effect and validate all unrelated failure-path payload fields. Explain at-least-once delivery, retention and audit limits, lease clock assumptions, manual operational decisions and why this is a small teaching queue, not an Azure/RabbitMQ implementation.

title: Tiến hóa schema sự kiện và upcasting không sửa lịch sử
requirements: Build independent producer/event-owner and consumer HTTP processes with separate SQLite databases. The owner keeps immutable bounded raw integration events with identity, ordered source position, explicit schema revision and bounded JSON payload. The consumer applies a deterministic v1-to-v2 upcaster into one canonical model; preserve event identity/source position and never rewrite historical producer records. A suggested example makes v1 integer totalCents explicitly USD and v2 nested amountMinor/currency, so the v1 currency default is a documented historical invariant, never a guess.

Write pure runtime parsing/upcasting and in-memory SQLite unit tests first for both supported revisions, invalid shapes/types/unsafe numbers, deterministic conversion, immutable inputs and unknown revisions. Distinguish schema revision from source sequence and business-resource version. Unknown/incompatible revisions fail closed without advancing the consumer checkpoint. Apply the canonical effect, durable deduplication fingerprint and checkpoint atomically; define conflicting reuse of an event ID explicitly. Bound pages, source retention and all HTTP operations; no dynamic code/schema loading or silent skipping of unknown records.

With real processes prove mixed v1/v2 records yield the same intended business meaning, the producer raw history stays unchanged, duplicate delivery does not reapply effects, conflicting identity is rejected, and an older consumer profile stops on v2 before a supported upgraded profile resumes after restart without losing/double-counting earlier events. Test unknown-version and malformed-history rejection with valid surrounding envelopes. Explain additive versus breaking changes, explicit defaults, upcaster-chain maintenance and rollout order. Keep this about event-format evolution, not a second CQRS/event-sourcing framework.

title: Phân trang keyset, snapshot hữu hạn và checkpoint tiếp tục
requirements: Build independent resource-owner and scanner HTTP processes with separate SQLite stores. The owner serves a keyset-paginated snapshot ordered by a unique immutable key using an indexed seek rather than OFFSET. Limit the demo to100 live resources,8 concurrent snapshots,10 rows per page and a documented finite TTL. Snapshot creation atomically copies the selected bounded data inside the owner store, so later inserts/updates/deletes cannot cause omissions, duplicates or changed values in that scan.

Use opaque locally generated random continuation tokens backed by immutable server-side session/position records; tokens bind filter and page size, are never interpreted as URLs or SQL by the scanner, and replaying one token returns the same page without allocating unbounded new cursor records. Persist sessions/tokens so restart behavior is explicit; expiry/unknown cursors and mismatched filters fail with documented contracts rather than silently starting a new scan. Scanner stores each page result and its next checkpoint atomically in its own SQLite; retries after an uncertain page/commit outcome must not skip or double-apply rows. Bound scans, response bytes and total/page deadlines. Unit-test injected-clock expiry boundaries, seeks, binding, replay and capacity first.

With real processes and barriers prove a scan sees the initial snapshot while source rows are inserted/deleted/changed between pages, every selected key appears exactly once, and scanner restart resumes the same valid checkpoint. Inject a page-application interruption before commit and prove a retry is safe; test owner restart, token expiry/malformed tokens and full snapshot capacity. Explain snapshot storage cost, finite retention, wall-clock assumptions and deliberate new-scan semantics after expiry. Do not claim keyset pagination alone gives snapshot isolation or implement Graph/OData.

title: Anti-corruption layer và chuyển đổi ngữ nghĩa hệ thống cũ
requirements: Build independent legacy provider, anti-corruption adapter and domain Orders/quote HTTP processes. The legacy provider uses a deliberately different wire/domain model: legacy SKU aliases, decimal-string unit prices, pack quantities and status codes. The adapter alone maps to a validated canonical product model with integer-cent prices, currency, available units and explicit availability; Orders uses only that canonical contract. Keep monetary data simulated with no payment integration or external APIs.

Write pure translation/validation unit tests first for exact decimal-to-integer conversion without floating rounding, safe integer overflow, pack-to-unit bounds, mismatched product identities, missing/ambiguous fields, unsupported currencies/statuses and documented not-found/unavailable mapping. Reject unknown semantics instead of inventing defaults or treating dependency failure as zero stock. Bound and validate every upstream response, use fixed trusted loopback origins and deadlines, and do not follow redirects. Keep legacy identifiers, status branching and conversion rules out of Orders.

Use real independent processes to prove valid translation and quote totals, missing product behavior, malformed/ambiguous legacy data rejection, transient provider failure/deadline and recovery. Include controlled legacy-format/scenario changes that leave the public domain contract stable without modifying consumer code. Teaching-control endpoints may be explicitly enabled for deterministic fixtures and Playground scenarios. Explain added latency, adapter ownership, mapping maintenance and the difference from gateway aggregation, API field renaming and Strangler ownership migration; do not claim the adapter repairs contradictory business data.

title: Request hedging cho GET, ngân sách tải và hủy nhánh thua
requirements: Build independent hedging-client and two read-only replica HTTP processes (replicas may share one entrypoint). Start one primary GET immediately; launch at most one secondary after a finite hedge delay when the primary is unresolved. Use the first valid successful response, cancel outstanding attempts and enforce one overall deadline. Only explicit safe read routes may hedge; reject POST/other unsafe mutations before forwarding. Describe this as an original bounded HTTP teaching policy inspired by hedging, not a gRPC implementation.

Write deterministic unit assertions first using an injected scheduler/clock and deferred promises for a fast primary suppressing the hedge, delayed secondary winning, nonfatal failures, fatal response policy, all attempts failing, deadline/disconnect cancellation and ignored late results. Validate bounded upstream bodies and logical resource identity before accepting a winner. Define which HTTP failures are fatal versus eligible for the second attempt; never allow an early transient error to mask a still-possible valid result. Bound per-operation attempts at2 and process-wide concurrent extra hedge attempts with a non-queuing skip policy; every path releases timers, permits and abort listeners.

With real separate replicas and synchronization barriers prove fast-primary sends one request, a held primary lets the secondary win, losing work observes cancellation and active counts return to0, caller disconnect/deadline cancels all branches, malformed success is not accepted, and hedge-capacity saturation cannot create an unbounded queue. Use counters/observable barriers rather than elapsed-time race guesses. Explain tail latency versus average latency, duplicated read cost, best-effort cancellation, consistency requirements between replicas and the distinction from sequential retry, bulkheads and circuit breakers. Use only loopback demo replicas and no external network.

title: Consumer-driven contracts và kiểm chứng provider tương thích
requirements: Build independent provider, consumer and contract-verifier HTTP processes. The consumer owns a small static typed interaction catalogue in .mts (not an extra JSON file), describing requests and the minimal response fields/statuses it actually uses. The provider must not import consumer contracts or matching rules. Use fixed bounded product-found and product-missing scenarios and show both consumer behavior and provider verification. This is an original built-in-only teaching verifier, not Pact or a compatible Pact format.

Write meaningful unit assertions first for request construction and response matching: required field absence/type changes/status changes fail, permitted additive fields pass, invalid primitive types and unknown interactions reject. Reuse the actual consumer request builder/parser in its contract checks rather than returning canned reports; keep independent provider fixtures so sharing an implementation cannot make both sides tautologically pass. The verifier accepts only configured loopback origin, never a caller URL; bound interactions, request/response bytes and total/per-request deadlines. Failure reports identify interaction and mismatch without exposing secrets.

With real separate processes prove compatible and additive provider revisions pass verification and the consumer still computes the intended value; breaking removal/type/status changes fail verification and consumer parsing. Include inspectable bounded teaching scenarios gated TEACHING_CONTROLS=1, recovery and inert-import tests. Explain consumer versus provider ownership, provider states, contract tests versus unit/integration/end-to-end tests, and that passing contracts do not prove business correctness or authorize deployment.

title: NDJSON streaming, backpressure và hủy luồng có giới hạn
requirements: Build independent HTTP NDJSON producer and consuming service processes. Producer streams at most64 bounded records plus an explicit terminal record; consumer validates ordered unique sequence, schema and terminal completion across arbitrary UTF-8/chunk boundaries. Keep each encoded line at most2048 bytes and the full stream at most131072 bytes; derive compatible limits including JSON escaping. Return a bounded JSON summary only after a complete valid stream; truncation, malformed records and missing terminal cannot be reported as successful partial results.

Write pure parser and injected-writer unit assertions first. A write returning false must stop pulling/generating records until drain; error, close, caller abort and deadline must remove listeners and release admission. Bound application buffers, concurrent streams (max2) and overall/per-read deadlines. Real server high-water mark may be configured with Node built-ins so a bounded response deterministically exercises write(false); document application versus kernel/transport buffering, and do not claim TCP memory is controlled by a JavaScript queue limit. No top-level listeners or external stream packages.

With real processes and observable barriers/counters prove complete streaming, real write(false)/drain handling, cancellation cleanup and saturation rejection. Failure fixtures for oversized lines/streams must satisfy unrelated schema/sequence fields, and malformed/truncated teaching modes must be explicit and gated TEACHING_CONTROLS=1. Test split UTF-8, boundary lengths, delayed drain, close while waiting, invalid terminal and restart/import cleanup. Explain streaming versus buffered JSON, bounded backpressure, at-most-in-flight work after cancellation and why streaming alone provides no replay/exactly-once guarantee.

title: Leader lease, fencing token và chặn leader cũ ghi dữ liệu
requirements: Build independent durable SQLite lease coordinator, two worker processes sharing one worker entrypoint, and a separate durable fenced sink. Coordinator grants one named leadership lease to a bounded holder identity, allocates a strictly increasing fencing generation, renews/releases only the exact current holder+generation while valid, and persists generations across restart. Workers make explicit bounded acquire/renew/write calls; no background election polling or external consensus system is required.

Write injected-clock/in-memory SQLite unit assertions first for exact expiry boundary, concurrent-style conditional grants, stale renew/release, monotonic restart generations and sink fencing. Sink atomically remembers the highest accepted generation and rejects lower generations before applying an idempotent operation receipt. Bind operation identity to immutable payload; duplicate replay cannot apply effects again, conflicting reuse rejects, and retained receipts have a finite admission bound. Crucial boundary: fencing stops older writes after the sink has observed a newer generation, not automatically at lease expiry or the instant a new grant is issued. Document the trusted non-Byzantine loopback participants; a generation is not an authentication credential.

With real processes prove only one current lease, takeover after expiry, stale-renew rejection, newer-generation sink activation followed by rejected stale-worker write, deduplication and coordinator/sink restart. Prefer explicit gated TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 clock-advance/stale-worker simulation or observable barriers over sleep races; keep normal paths checking their lease and controls clearly local-only. Bound HTTP bodies, calls, leases and storage. Explain clock assumptions, paused workers, single-coordinator availability and why this is not Raft/Kubernetes/production distributed locking.

title: Reconciliation và sửa read model khi mất thông báo
requirements: Build independent authoritative resource-owner, durable SQLite projection and manual reconciliation HTTP processes. Owner retains at most16 resource identities including tombstones, with monotonic per-resource versions and bounded values. A bounded atomic full snapshot (not another pagination framework) provides authoritative current state including deletions; dropping a notification must not lose this source of truth. Focus on pull anti-entropy repair beyond lesson15 normal event delivery.

Write unit assertions first for monotonic idempotent projection apply, duplicate versions, stale updates, same-version conflicting payload and tombstone protection. Repair only older/missing states; never silently overwrite an equal-version conflict or resurrect a newer deletion. Reconciliation accepts only configured origins, reads one bounded validated snapshot and applies at most16 repairs with bounded concurrency/deadlines/bytes. Partial repair failure may leave already applied records; repeated full runs safely converge without pretending there is a cross-service transaction. Report conflicts explicitly and document finite tombstone retention/admission.

With real processes prove a deliberately dropped update/deletion is detected and repaired, rerunning applies no duplicate changes, stale notifications after repair are ignored, and owner/projection restarts preserve versions and deletion state. Include dependency failure, partial progress/retry and an observable equal-version-conflict case using narrowly gated teaching controls if necessary. Explain desired/current state, periodic scheduling as an operational choice (manual /run is sufficient), repair lag, authority and why reconciliation neither replaces an outbox nor repairs contradictory equal-version business data automatically.

title: Cô lập tenant trong context, truy vấn và idempotency
requirements: Build independent demo gateway and durable document-service HTTP processes. Gateway maps two explicitly simulated principals to two tenants and signs a bounded tenant context with a locally generated Ed25519 key; document service independently verifies pinned public key, issuer/audience, expiry and primitive tenant/subject claims. Native commands generate ephemeral demo keys with Node; no external credentials or identity service. For Playground use private/public PEM environment values (the existing manager supports $auth.private and $auth.public). The demo principal selector is enabled only by TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 and must be described as simulated identity, not real login security.

Write pure context validation and in-memory SQLite isolation assertions first. Resolve tenant exclusively from verified context; raw x-tenant headers, query/body tenant overrides, missing/tampered/expired/wrong-audience context cannot select storage. Every document read/list/write and idempotency receipt uses tenant-qualified keys. Both tenants can reuse the same document ID and operation ID independently; replay deduplicates only within that tenant and conflicts remain local. Bound at20 documents and40 retained operation receipts per tenant with explicit full-capacity rejection, not unsafe receipt eviction. No process-global mutable current-tenant state or unqualified shared cache keys.

With real independent processes prove scoped reads/lists/writes, cross-tenant guessed IDs indistinguishable from missing, same IDs and receipts in both tenants without leakage, conflicting payload replay inside one tenant, concurrent mixed-tenant requests and durable isolation after restart. Test spoofed tenant hints, signed-context validation failures and one tenants capacity not blocking the others admitted writes. Bound headers/bodies/upstream responses and deadlines. Explain authentication versus tenant authorization, shared-table isolation tradeoffs, demonstration identity boundary and why signatures alone cannot fix a missing tenant predicate.

title: Consistent hashing, virtual nodes và affinity khi đổi membership
requirements: Create router.mts plus node.mts (three independent node instances a,b,c), pure ring/cache modules and Vietnamese README/tests. Router has fixed NODE_A_ORIGIN/NODE_B_ORIGIN/NODE_C_ORIGIN; nodes use NODE_ID. Build a deterministic SHA-256 clockwise ring with16 virtual tokens per member, canonical collision tie-break, wraparound and at most3 fixed members. Normal membership starts a,b. GET /objects/:key routes to exactly the owner, validates bounded reply and returns owner/cache-hit information; node caches at most32 keys with safe LRU eviction. Values must be deterministic recomputable demo catalogue data, not authoritative mutable storage. State clearly that this teaches cache affinity: membership changes do NOT migrate durable data and provide no replication, consensus or automatic availability.

Write meaningful pure unit failures first: deterministic mapping independent of member input order, explicit wrap/tie fixtures, adding c moves only keys now owned by c, removing b moves only keys previously owned by b, maximal identities and LRU eviction/recompute. With TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 router accepts POST /ring {members:[...]} with unique nonempty subset of a,b,c; otherwise control is absent. GET /placement/:key exposes bounded current owner and ring epoch; no caller URLs, no unbounded mappings/history. Invalid member arrays/types/duplicates rejected. A changed ring does not silently route around an unavailable owner: return502 with deadline and no second-owner request.

Real independent-process HTTP tests prove warm affinity, adding/removing a node, unchanged-owner cache hits, moved-key cold reconstruction with identical value, unavailable owner and restart clearing only cache, disabled controls, schema/byte/deadline bounds and inert imports. Demonstrate movement counts for a fixed bounded key sample against modulo hashing without claiming universal balance or guaranteed exact movement percentages. Explain virtual nodes versus physical nodes, hot keys, uneven load, stale membership, cache cold start and the extra migration protocol required for stateful shards. Keep all replies bounded including maximal escaping.

title: Thứ tự sự kiện theo partition và checkpoint không vượt qua khoảng trống
requirements: Build durable broker.mts and consumer.mts with SQLite (consumer can run twice with separate DBs); pure routing/checkpoint model first. Broker maps a bounded key deterministically to one of3 fixed partitions, assigns contiguous offsets per partition, appends POST /events {id,key,delta} and exposes GET /events?partition=P&after=N&limit=L (L1..8). Retain max16 distinct keys globally and32 events per partition, no unsafe eviction. Repeated global event id with identical key/delta returns the original partition/offset; changed payload conflicts409. Delta is a bounded nonzero safe integer, aggregate bounds explicit. No broker package or Kafka emulation claim.

Consumer POST /deliver accepts the complete broker event and atomically updates projection plus partition checkpoint only when offset==checkpoint+1. Gap returns409 with expected offset and performs zero effects; no unbounded buffer. Duplicate old offset succeeds only when retained event identity/payload exactly match; altered old data or reused id at another offset conflicts. Verify key-to-partition consistency. Bound projections to the16 admitted keys and receipts to96 events. POST /poll {partition} fetches a bounded batch from configured BROKER_ORIGIN (no caller URL), validates the complete envelope and contiguous order before applying, with explicit per-request/total deadlines; GET /state reports three checkpoints and key balances. Busy admission is bounded and must not make one partition gap block valid deliveries to another.

First observe unit assertion failures for gap handling, duplicate/conflict, independent partitions and atomic balance/checkpoint updates using in-memory SQLite. Real HTTP tests prove out-of-order delivery is rejected then recoverable by poll, another partition progresses, broker idempotency, two independent consumers/cursors, concurrent mixed-key requests, consumer/broker restart durability, full retention rejection, malformed/oversized upstream yields no partial batch effects, deadlines, disabled/inert entrypoints and guaranteed cleanup. Explain ordering scope, hot partitions, head-of-line blocking, offset commit versus external side effects, lack of rebalance/consumer-group protocol and why changing partition count needs a migration plan.

title: Try–Confirm–Cancel, đặt giữ tài nguyên và khôi phục quyết định bền vững
requirements: Create coordinator.mts and participant.mts (inventory and wallet demo-credit instances), independent SQLite per process; no real payment. Participant configuration RESOURCE and CAPACITY, coordinator INVENTORY_ORIGIN/WALLET_ORIGIN, all DB_PATH. POST participant /try,/confirm,/cancel bind {id,units} to one durable reservation; held/confirmed/cancelled states and idempotent terminal results, conflicting payload or illegal transition409. Confirm held consumes once; cancel held releases once. Cancel-before-try creates a retained cancellation tombstone so late Try cannot reserve. Never expire participant holds autonomously: once a durable commit decision exists, expiry must not destroy the promised resource. Max16 retained reservation identities per participant including tombstones, no unsafe eviction; capacity/available/held/consumed observable via GET /state.

Coordinator POST /transactions {id,quantity,amount}, GET /transactions/:id and POST /recover {id}. Bind request id to payload durably before Try, max16 transactions; reserve both resources, then persist commit decision BEFORE sending any Confirm. On Try failure/uncertainty persist abort decision and send Cancel to BOTH participants, including one whose Try outcome is unknown. Recover an undecided transaction conservatively by durable abort and cancellation of both. Once committing, never cancel or switch the decision: repeated recovery rolls forward until both confirms acknowledged. Failed phase delivery leaves explicit202 pending state; committed/aborted terminal states are durable and repeated commands idempotent. Bound concurrent coordinator operations with explicit busy status, all upstream requests/replies/deadlines, redirect:error and runtime parsing. No unbounded background recovery queue.

Write unit RED/GREEN for balance conservation, idempotency, conflicting replay, empty rollback tombstone and late Try rejection, durable commit/abort transitions. Real independent-process HTTP tests cover success/replay, second Try insufficient funds releasing the first hold, Cancel-before-Try, disabled controls, partial Confirm via a bounded participant failure control gated TEACHING_CONTROLS=1, restart coordinator after persisted decision then forward recovery, abort/cancel recovery, independent participant restart, no double consumption, capacities and malformed/oversized replies. Controls may return503 for selected Try/Confirm/Cancel phases but must not skip state invariants. Explain coordinator crash before/after decision, retained tombstones, stalled holds requiring operator recovery, TCC versus saga compensation and the lack of atomic visibility/consensus under partitions. Do not claim all-or-nothing instantaneous visibility across independent stores.

title: Read-your-writes bằng version barrier và replica fallback có giới hạn
requirements: Create primary.mts, replica.mts and gateway.mts with separate durable primary/replica SQLite stores. Primary POST /items/:id {value} commits a bounded item and monotonic safe global commitVersion atomically, returns {item,commitVersion}; max16 identities, value<=256 UTF-16 units, ids ASCII<=64. Primary GET /snapshot gives one bounded atomic full snapshot of items plus commitVersion. Best-effort push to fixed REPLICA_ORIGIN applies a complete snapshot, never partial per-row watermark. Replica POST /snapshot atomically replaces state and watermark only for strictly newer valid snapshot; exact replay is duplicate, equal-version different content conflicts, older snapshots cannot roll back any item. GET /items/:id supports optional minVersion safe nonnegative integer; lag returns425 before returning data, sufficiently current missing item404.

Gateway configured PRIMARY_ORIGIN/REPLICA_ORIGIN forwards writes and supports GET /items/:id?minVersion=N. Try replica once; if its explicit425 lag result occurs, try primary once under one total deadline. Primary must enforce the same minimum barrier: an unavailable primary or impossible future version must never yield stale success. Casual read without token may use stale replica; with a token N it must return state at least N or an explicit error. Include source/watermark metadata so behavior is observable, and runtime-validate successful/failure upstream replies including watermark>=requested barrier. Token is only a minimum version for this one persistent primary history, not a credential, historical snapshot selector, cross-database epoch or global causal consistency guarantee. Document that deleting/replacing DB invalidates this token scope.

Observe pure/in-memory unit RED/GREEN for monotonic commit/version, atomic snapshot validation/apply, no watermark advance on invalid/partial snapshot, equal-version conflict, strict minVersion parsing and fallback decisions. TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 may hold/release replication and trigger explicit POST /replicate; no arbitrary URL or silent data reset. Real processes prove stale casual read, replica425 for a write token, gateway fallback returning own write, subsequent replication serving the token from replica, older-token latest-state behavior, future-token failure, dependency unavailability/deadline, invalid/oversized snapshot zero writes, and primary/replica restart retaining barriers. Bound request/snapshot bytes including16 maximally escaped values and canonical equality independent of item input order; explain availability/latency cost and limits versus lesson15 CQRS.

title: Feature flags, cohort ổn định và cấu hình rollout có hạn dùng
requirements: Build control.mts (durable SQLite one-flag control plane), gateway.mts (two independent instances) and backend.mts (stable/canary variants). Control GET /config returns a bounded versioned configuration for one fixed flag: enabled boolean, rollout integer0..10000, salt bounded string; POST /config publishes against explicit expectedVersion, increments durable safe version, rejects conflicts/types. Config contains NO target URL. Gateway has fixed CONTROL_ORIGIN/STABLE_ORIGIN/CANARY_ORIGIN and bounded local single-snapshot cache, explicit POST /refresh and GET /hello?subject=ID. Bucket is deterministic SHA-256(salt+delimiter+subject) mapped into0..9999; equal configuration and subject must choose the same variant across gateway instances. This subject is a demo routing key, not authenticated identity or authorization.

Start with stable/default when no valid config. A good refresh accepts newer version, rejects equal-version conflicting content and older versions, and sets last-success age; repeated exact config can refresh age. Failed/malformed/oversized/redirected refresh must not overwrite the last known good config or extend its age. Within TTL serve cached decision; once stale use stable with an explicit fallback reason until a valid refresh. Use monotonic age and injected clock in pure tests; optional bounded POST /teaching/advance gated TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 makes expiry deterministic in real HTTP, TTL default10000ms. Gate control-plane failure injection similarly. Disabled flag overrides rollout; a kill switch takes effect only after each gateway refreshes or its TTL expires, not instantly fleet-wide. Selected backend errors return explicit502 rather than inventing successful business data.

Observe unit assertion RED/GREEN for deterministic cohort vectors,0/100% boundaries, monotonic rollout property with unchanged salt, version/conflict rules, failed-refresh age, exact TTL boundary and fallback. Real independent processes prove two gateways agree for a bounded subject sample, changing rollout/salt, durable config restart, gateway cold restart, disabled flag, one stale gateway after a kill switch, last-known-good during a control outage then stable fallback after a teaching clock advance, failed refresh not extending TTL, invalid primitive inputs, bounded upstream bytes/deadlines and no signed/context/body forwarding on redirect. All modules inert; max one flag/config cache, bounded subjects/headers and no arbitrary per-user maps. Explain release versus deploy, cohort bias, salt changes, eventual configuration convergence, flag cleanup and why this is not an A/B analytics platform or security feature.

title: CRDT PN-counter, cập nhật độc lập và hội tụ khi trao đổi trạng thái
requirements: Create replica.mts (three instances ACTOR_ID=a,b,c, independent DB_PATH) and sync.mts with fixed REPLICA_A_ORIGIN/B/C, pure model and SQLite store. One state-based PN-counter has exactly three fixed actor components for positive and negative counts; each coordinate integer0..1000000, value=sum(P)-sum(N). A local POST /changes {id,delta} changes ONLY its own positive or negative component, delta nonzero integer -1000..1000. Persist state plus max16 local idempotency receipts atomically: same id/payload replays, changed delta409, capacity/coordinate overflow409 without effects. Persist actor identity in the DB and reject reopening it under a different actor. No reset or dynamic actor membership.

GET /state exposes actor, complete state and derived value. POST /merge accepts a complete parsed state and atomically applies componentwise max; duplicate, delayed and reordered state messages cannot double count or decrease coordinates. Reject missing/extra actors, wrong primitives, unsafe/out-of-bound coordinates before any write. The sync service POST /sync {from,to} accepts only distinct fixed actor IDs, reads from the configured source once and merges to the configured destination once; parse bounded envelopes, validate advertised actor and derived value, use total deadlines and redirect:error. It is explicit exchange, not an unbounded gossip worker; no caller URLs. SQLite contains one state and16 local receipts, no growing operation history.

Observe meaningful unit RED/GREEN for commutative/associative/idempotent merge, independent concurrent changes, monotone coordinates with negative displayed values, overflow, conflicting replay and atomic rejection. Real independent-process tests prove divergence while disconnected, exchange/reordered old snapshots yielding convergence, duplicate sync, durable restarts/actor mismatch, independent local command replay, retention rejection, malformed/oversized upstream zero effects, deadlines/redirects and inert imports with cleanup. Explain trusted single-writer-per-actor and eventual delivery assumptions; deleting/restoring actor storage can lose updates, forged coordinates are not prevented by this unauthenticated demo. A PN-counter does NOT enforce nonnegative stock, global uniqueness or linearizability; compare with lesson33 fencing and38 reservations.

title: Webhook có chữ ký trên raw body, chống replay cũ và xử lý giao trùng
requirements: Build publisher.mts and receiver.mts with independent SQLite DB_PATH and explicitly configured public demo WEBHOOK_SECRET (32..128 ASCII characters, never use real credentials). Publisher POST /events {id,delta} durably retains max16 immutable demo events (id ASCII1..64, delta nonzero integer -100..100), same payload replay idempotent, changed payload409. POST /deliver {id} makes one bounded attempt to fixed RECEIVER_ORIGIN /webhook; max8 attempts per event and one active delivery with explicit busy response, no background retry queue. Generate a fresh Unix-seconds timestamp and HMAC-SHA256 signature for EVERY attempt over ASCII timestamp + dot + exact retained raw JSON bytes. Headers x-demo-timestamp and x-demo-signature use strict canonical digits and64 lowercase hex. Publisher GET /events/:id exposes bounded delivery state/attempts; receiver GET /state exposes total and retained receipt count for observing uncertain delivery.

Receiver reads a bounded raw byte body BEFORE JSON interpretation, verifies HMAC with timingSafeEqual after length/format validation, and permits timestamps within inclusive60 seconds of its injected/current clock. Missing/bad/stale/future credentials403 without effects; malformed/oversized input has explicit400/413. Parse only after authentication, bind event id to canonical payload and atomically store receipt plus bounded total in SQLite. Exact semantic event replay acknowledges without another delta; conflicting authenticated id409; retain max16 receipts, reject new beyond cap instead of unsafe eviction. Publisher must runtime-validate bounded acknowledgments before marking delivered. A lost reply after receiver commit leaves uncertainty and is recovered by idempotent redelivery with a new timestamp/signature. redirect:error; never follow caller URLs.

First observe unit assertion RED/GREEN for known HMAC vectors/raw-byte tampering, strict timestamp/signature types, exact freshness boundaries, receipt/effect atomicity and payload conflicts. Real processes prove delivery, duplicate redelivery, signed byte tamper, expired/future replay, receiver restart, bounded retention and malformed/oversized acknowledgments/deadlines/redirects. For a deterministic Playground demonstration, TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 on receiver may enable POST /teaching/failure {afterCommit:boolean}: when true a newly applied event responds503 AFTER commit, while an authenticated duplicate still acknowledges normally; disabled controls404 and invalid primitives400. Unit clocks are injected; optional gated bounded clock advance for HTTP freshness tests. No real Stripe/payment/external endpoint. Explain signature integrity versus encryption, clock skew, at-least-once delivery, event ordering and key rotation/secret distribution as production concerns; local HTTP/public demo secret provide no production security.

title: Upload nhiều phần có thể tiếp tục, checksum và công bố đối tượng nguyên tử
requirements: Create upload.mts durable SQLite object owner and reader.mts independent HTTP read facade using fixed STORE_ORIGIN. A custom bounded teaching protocol, NOT S3/Tus compatibility. POST /uploads {uploadId,parts,size,sha256} binds ASCII1..32 id to immutable metadata; parts1..8, size1..8192 and feasible for1..1024 bytes per part, digest64 lowercase hex. Max16 retained upload identities including aborted/completed, no unsafe eviction. GET /uploads/:id returns status and sorted bounded received-part metadata so a client can resume after restart. Same create metadata is idempotent and never resets progress; conflicts409.

PUT /uploads/:id/parts/:number accepts {base64,sha256}; strict canonical base64 decodes1..1024 bytes and SHA256 must match raw bytes. Part numbers1..declared count, immutable after first acceptance: exact replay succeeds, changed bytes/hash409. Validate every field/byte bound before transactional writes. POST /uploads/:id/complete requires every contiguous part, total declared size and full concatenated SHA256; atomically publishes complete state/object in SQLite, idempotent exact completion, incomplete or wrong full digest409 without exposing partial bytes. DELETE /uploads/:id aborts open uploads, releases staged blobs but retains tombstone; duplicate abort succeeds, completed abort409 and late parts cannot resurrect an aborted id. GET /objects/:id exposes only completed {id,base64,size,sha256}; reader GET /objects/:id validates full bounded upstream schema/canonical bytes/size/digest before responding, missing404 versus invalid502, total deadline and redirect:error.

Observe unit RED/GREEN for out-of-order parts/resume metadata, exact duplicate/conflict, canonical base64 and checksum failures, incomplete/full-checksum rejection, atomic publication, abort tombstone and capacity. Real independent-process tests prove part2 before1, crash/restart retaining parts, retry skipped received parts, reader404 before complete and verified200 after, completion replay, abort/restart/late part failure, maximal8x1024 legal upload and byte budgets including base64 expansion, schema-valid oversized bodies, malformed/oversized/slow/redirected provider zero partial success, inert imports and guaranteed cleanup. No arbitrary file paths, cloud storage or extra dependencies: SQLite BLOBs keep the tiny demo bounded. Explain chunk versus full checksum, storage reclamation/tombstone retention, why changing a committed part requires a new upload, quotas, abandoned uploads, authorization and lack of streaming/large-file scalability.

title: URL cấp quyền theo đối tượng, thời hạn và tiêu thụ một lần bền vững
requirements: Build issuer.mts and objects.mts with separate SQLite DB_PATH and explicitly configured public demo CAPABILITY_SECRET (32..128 ASCII). Fixed immutable bounded catalogue IDs doc,photo,report with small original demo contents. Issuer POST /tickets {requestId,objectId,ttlSeconds} accepts ASCII1..32 requestId, known object and integerTTL1..60; max16 retained issues, binds immutable request metadata and expiry durably. Same issue request returns original ticket/expiry without extending it; changed object/TTL409. Ticket format is canonical base64url(JSON.stringify([1,"objects-demo","GET",objectId,expiresAt,requestId])) + dot +64 lowercase HMAC-SHA256 hex over that base64url segment. Return a relative /objects/:id?ticket=... path, expiry and requestId; no caller origins or target URLs.

Objects GET /objects/:id?ticket=... bounds token/query/header lengths, verifies signature with timingSafeEqual after format/length checks, parses exact tuple/types/canonical encoding, audience, method, object binding and expiry (now < expiresAt). Missing/forged/wrong-scope/expired tickets403; repeated query invalid400; unsupported method405 must not consume. A valid grant is consumed transactionally once in a max16 retained spent-ID registry before returning its object; reuse409 including after restart, no eviction or raw tokens in logs. Invalid/expired/wrong-object requests do zero effects. After a successful consume with lost response, automatic retry cannot recover the object: document this explicit one-use tradeoff. Reject capacity safely. Issuer is a local unauthenticated educational mint, not a production authorization service.

Observe unit RED/GREEN for known signature/canonical vectors, token tamper, strict tuple/primitive parsing, audience/path/method binding, exact expiry boundary, immutable issuance replay, one-use transaction and bounds. Real processes prove issued grant, wrong object then correct use, first200/replay409, object-store and issuer restart, expired/future-invalid schema, altered token, duplicate query, retention and no token logging; all modules inert and cleanup guaranteed. TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 may enable bounded positive POST /teaching/advance {seconds} and TEACHING_EPOCH_SECONDS fixed initial time on both processes for repeatable local UI; reject fixed clock without controls, default uses real Unix time, invalid controls400 and absent controls404. Explain bearer delegation, synchronized-clock/trusted-secret assumptions, leakage via URLs/referrers/logs, HTTPS, issuer authentication, key rotation and lack of revocation before expiry. Never claim this custom one-use demo implements AWS presigned URL semantics (those can be reused until expiry).

title: Traffic shadowing, so sánh bản mới và giới hạn tải quan sát
requirements: Create gateway.mts with fixed PRIMARY_ORIGIN/SHADOW_ORIGIN and backend.mts instantiated as primary/shadow using ordinary VARIANT. GET /products/:id accepts ASCII1..32 id, no extra query, retrieves/validates bounded primary {id,price,currency:"VND"} and returns ONLY that business result. A successful primary read may start one sanitized GET to the shadow: fixed path/id, explicit allowlisted headers, no caller authorization/cookies/signed context/query/body. Never mirror mutations, invalid requests or failed primary replies. Shadow output is compared on id/price/currency but never determines the caller response. All origins reject redirects, requests/replies have byte/deadline contracts; invalid primary502, primary deadline504, shadow failure never manufactures business data.

Mirror work must not be awaited by the user response. Bound active mirror tasks to2 with no pending queue; extra requests still use primary and increment a skipped counter. Each mirror has its own bounded deadline and cleanup in finally, including client disconnect/server shutdown; no unhandled rejection. GET /stats returns bounded active/started/skipped/matched/mismatched/failed counters (saturate at1000000) and at most one last comparison, never raw request or unbounded per-subject history. TEACHING_CONTROLS=1 may add POST gateway /teaching/drain to await only a snapshot of at most2 outstanding tasks under a deadline and return stats. Shadow backend may gate POST /teaching/behavior {mode:"same"|"different"|"unavailable"} and /teaching/hold {enabled:boolean} with at most2 held replies and explicit release; controls absent404 and invalid primitives400.

Observe meaningful pure unit RED/GREEN for comparator validation, mirror permit2/drop policy, release on every settlement and saturating counters. Real independent processes prove matching/mismatching shadow while primary data unchanged, control-induced outage, no auth/context/body forwarding including redirects, no shadow call for POST or invalid/failed primary, and max2 concurrent held mirrors with extra admission skipped. Prove nonblocking response with an observable barrier: primary caller completes while shadow replies remain held; elapsed-time-only assertions are insufficient. Release/timeout/drain must restore active0. Test invalid/oversized/slow upstream, bounded last comparison, disabled controls, inert imports and guaranteed process/held-request cleanup. Explain shadowing versus canary routing and hedged reads, side-effect safety even for GET, PII/data minimization, extra capacity cost, sampling and limits of semantic comparison; no production traffic or deployment.
